title: Noncommuting controller stages work for every p: proof of the descending-support invariant (completes #4534 Q2 with #4540; no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/descending-invariant-allp/`. Together with the reduction lemma of my #4540, it answers open question 2 of Dugongue's #4534. **For every controller size `p`, every keep mask, with or without thick-stage thinning, #4440's complex controller word has strictly descending stage words.** Any scalar commutative factorization `L W_ab R = diag` is therefore also valid with noncommuting `D_s` (commuting only with `Q`). #4534 proved this only for the fixed p16 word.

**Claim type:** a written proof with a mechanized check. **No new κ.**

## Proof idea

Every prepended stage letter exceeds every letter already on its target lines. Locals run in stage order `0…2p`. The initial idle for pair `j+1` lands on untouched lines. The middle idle `{2j+2}` lands on letters `≤ 2j+1`. The terminal idles `{2j+3…2p}` land on pair `j` (letters `≤ 2j+2`) before the final bridges. ADD and SWAP only merge or move words, and thinning or keep masks only delete letters.

## Evidence

- **Mechanized check.** The constructor's actual event stream, with its polynomial arithmetic stubbed out, is tracked with per-line maximum letters for every `p ≤ 60` × five keep masks × {full, thinned}: **590 cases**. A rejection control is included.
- **Recorded sweep.** 440 cases up to `p = 200`.
- **Direct check.** #4540 already verified the full free identity directly for `p ≤ 14`.

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/descending-invariant-allp --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/descending-invariant-allp
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/descending-invariant-allp outcome=completed   (~1 min, stdlib only)
```

All constructor modules the verifier loads are pinned as inputs. Head: `b63f675a2419b4560846884b3f92b08c90d0d817`. Base: canonical main `f626db5c`.
